summary.tldr: Requires the federal health minister to create a national framework on fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, with measures on training, awareness, research, standards and reporting.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national framework on fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.
Includes measures for training, education and guidance for health care and other professionals on prevention, diagnosis and support.
Promotes research and information sharing between governments on prevention, diagnosis and support.

Sets national standards for prevention, diagnosis and support, and a strategy to raise awareness about alcohol use during pregnancy and fetal alcohol spectrum disorder risks, including possible changes to alcohol-related laws and policies.
Requires the minister to consult federal ministers, provinces and territories, stakeholders, Indigenous communities and others while developing the framework.
Requires a report on the framework to be tabled within one year, published online within 10 days, and followed by a five-year report on what was implemented and why any measures were not.
who_it_affects: People with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder
summary.background: The bill says the framework is meant to support Canadians with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, their families and their caregivers.
